correctness.rationale: The proof explicitly partitions factors into at least two ones, exactly one one, or no ones, and covers every case with the selected positions. For the lower bound, unique adjacent-one-gap factors at alternating gap scales have mutually disjoint occurrence intervals, augmented with one final-gap witness for even k or two separated boundary witnesses for odd k. Each zero-run uniqueness and endpoint inequality is checked for k>=2. Independent substring enumeration and interval disjointness passed for k=2..8 , but the mathematical proof is general. No finite test is claimed as an infinite certificate.

originality.rationale: The exact same base sequence appears in Schaeffer–Shallit Theorem 8, which gives only upper attractors for ranges of n and explicitly identifies matching lower bounds as needing other techniques. The new proof supplies a matching lower bound at all dyadic lengths, and an exact optimum. Published general Θ(log n) bounds and a previously known online greedy set do not imply optimal offline cardinality. No matching closed dyadic formula was found in queried public records, leaving a bibliographic risk.
residual_risks: Unindexed or later exact dyadic formula may exist; lack of search hit is not an absolute novelty proof.

value.rationale: The same natural sparse automatic word is a named primary example of a known nonconstant logarithmic string-attractor upper bound. The theorem gives a sharp exact offline invariant at every power-of-two prefix length, an infinite calibrated family of optimal witness sets, and an explicit factor-packing obstruction; this resolves a mathematically motivated missing lower bound, rather than an arbitrary small numerical improvement.
